source_snapshot.test_name_items: USB Hub Hot-Plug of all ports
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Plug USB Hub with USB device *2 on all USB ports.
2. Check all USB devices status.
3. Unplug all USB devices and check status again.
4. Repeat hot-plug steps at least 5 times for each port (Interval of each hot-plug time: 10 seconds)

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. All USB ports should be plugged devices successfully.
2. All USB devices should be detected and functional when plugged.
3. All information of USB devices should be removed when unplugged.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- repeated USB add/remove via the kernel is triggered by physical plug; agent reads `dmesg` USB enumeration after the operator hot-plugs. Agent part: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lsusb 2>&1; echo ---dmesg---; dmesg | grep -iE 'usb [0-9]|new.*usb' | tail -20 2>&1"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL `lsusb` list + dmesg USB enumeration lines so the user confirms the USB Hub Hot-Plug of all ports device(s) appear on the expected ports; the physical USB insertion/speed-transfer measurement is the operator part.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: physical USB insertion is operator; agent reads the enumeration/traffic evidence only.

original_test_intent: Verify every physical USB port supports repeated hot-plug of one hub populated with two devices, including detection, device function and complete removal across at least five 10-second cycles.
original_method: A qualified operator physically connects the approved hub and two-device fixture to each port, checks both downstream devices, safely disconnects the fixture, verifies topology removal and repeats the sequence.
manual_activity: Repeated hub insertion/removal at each connector is the core test stimulus, and an operator must also establish physical-port identity and device-specific function. Automated topology collection is corroboration, not execution of that core.
required_inputs: Approved powered/unpowered hub plus two-device identity/function matrix
Hub/device current demand and per-port power allowance
Removal semantics, safe mount/open-handle cleanup and interval definition
Qualified operator, recovery path and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Do not exceed port or hub power limits; stop on overcurrent, heat, connector damage or unstable enumeration.
Close writes, mounts and handles before unplugging any storage-class device.
Retain complete per-cycle event context rather than only tailing the last 20 lines.
Preserve the first failure and do not automatically replug or retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only full USB tree, hub/downstream descriptors, kernel events, mount state and host health around each operator action.
Correlate both downstream identities and functions to the physical port/cycle matrix.
Flag stale nodes, overcurrent and missing cycles without claiming hot-plug execution or PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the fixture, power budget and per-device functional checks.
Perform every physical insertion/removal and visually confirm connector identity.
Review evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: lsusb/dmesg are appropriate supporting observations, but a single list plus tail-20 log can omit the hub hierarchy, both functions and earlier cycles.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain physical hot-plug; use full platform-approved USB topology/event capture without truncating required cycle evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All ports, one hub with two devices, successful function and removal, at least five cycles, 10-second intervals and both five-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: RETAIN PHYSICAL HUB HOT-PLUG WITH FULL TOPOLOGY EVIDENCE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a port-by-cycle matrix with timestamped operator actions, hub and both downstream identities/functions, synchronized full topology/events and power/cleanup checks.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact chassis USB connectors, controller topology and approved hub/device combination.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record kernel, USB controller, hub and downstream device versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner port power specification, approved fixture list and OS safe-removal procedure.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds power, hierarchy, identity and evidence controls without replacing physical operations.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No loss; the hub and both devices remain required at every port and cycle.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Port map, fixture, power budget, functions and cleanup rule.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OS enumeration does not prove the exact connector, physical insertion or successful downstream function.

project_override_considerations: Projects may select the hub/device models and functional probes within the approved power budget, but may not reduce all-port, two-device, five-cycle or 10-second coverage without recording an explicit plan override.
expected_evidence: Approved port/hub/two-device map, current budget, functions, cleanup and authorization
Per-port/per-cycle physical timestamps and hub-plus-two-device topology
Separate functional results for both downstream devices and clean removal evidence
Overcurrent/kernel/host-health review, final topology and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure and criteria consistently require hub hot-plug, two-device function and removal; missing fixture and power details are readiness inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: An approved fixture and operator can satisfy the core test. It is MANUAL ONLY because the physical repeated stimulus is central, not because execution is impossible.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Change PARTIAL to MANUAL ONLY under locked V3.1 because repeated physical hot-plug is the core operation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain V2 power/safety/evidence improvements but change its PARTIAL classification for the same reason.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Prevents automated log collection from being mistaken for execution of the physical hub cycles.

review_improvement: Requires proof of hub hierarchy and both downstream functions for every connector and repetition, not a generic truncated enumeration snapshot.
independent_technical_reasoning: Unlike a one-time fixture setup followed by an automated workload, this procedure repeatedly moves and disconnects a populated hub on every port. Those human actions are the tested operation itself, so supporting USB telemetry does not make the case PARTIAL.
